title: xtralab launcher
description: Settings for the xtralab agent launcher.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: Override or extend the built-in list of agents shown on the launcher. Each entry must include an `id`. When the id matches a built-in (claude, codex, antigravity, copilot, goose, opencode, kiro, mistral-vibe), the fields you set override the corresponding defaults; leave a field out to keep the default. New ids define brand-new cards. Set `enabled: false` to hide a default. Changing a built-in's `command` (for example to a shell alias like `ccm`) keeps the card visible even though the alias isn't on PATH; use `requireAvailable: false` only when you want to skip the check without changing the command. The full built-in list is shown as the default below, so you can copy an entry and tweak it in place.

id.title: ID
id.description: Stable identifier. Match one of xtralab's defaults to override, or pick a new id to define a new card.

label.title: Label
label.description: Card title shown on the launcher.

caption.title: Caption
caption.description: Short description shown beneath the card title.

command.title: Command
command.description: Literal string typed into the new terminal. Aliases work because shells expand them on interactive lines.

iconSvg.title: Icon SVG
iconSvg.description: Inline SVG for the card icon. Required only for new agents whose icon is not already shipped by xtralab.

rank.title: Rank
rank.description: Sort order on the launcher (lower numbers come first).

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: When false, hides the agent from the launcher and command palette.

requireAvailable.title: Require available
requireAvailable.description: When false, the launcher skips the availability check for this entry (useful for shell aliases that aren't on PATH but resolve in an interactive shell). Overriding a built-in agent's command turns this off automatically, so an aliased command still shows; set it explicitly to force the check on or off.

promptArgs.title: Prompt arguments
promptArgs.description: How to splice an initial prompt from the launcher textarea into the agent's command line. Empty array (`[]`) appends the prompt as a positional argument. An array like `["-i"]` or `["--prompt"]` prefixes the prompt with that flag. Set to `null` to opt out of prompt support entirely (the agent's button is dimmed when the prompt textarea is non-empty).

editors.title: Editors
editors.description: Override or extend the terminal editors offered in the launcher's Open section (and recognized in the Terminals panel). Each entry must include an `id`. When the id matches a built-in (nvim, vim), the fields you set override the corresponding defaults; leave a field out to keep the default. New ids define additional editors. The launcher shows a single tile — the first editor, by `rank`, whose `command` is on PATH (Neovim before Vim by default). Set `enabled: false` to hide a built-in; disable both to remove the tile entirely. Changing a built-in's `command` (for example to a shell alias) keeps the tile visible even though the alias isn't on PATH; use `requireAvailable: false` only when you want to skip the check without changing the command. The full built-in list is shown as the default below, so you can copy an entry and tweak it in place.

id.title: ID
id.description: Stable identifier. Match a built-in (nvim, vim) to override, or pick a new id to define a new editor.

label.title: Label
label.description: Tile title shown on the launcher.

command.title: Command
command.description: Literal string typed into the new terminal (e.g. `nvim`). Aliases work because shells expand them on interactive lines.

iconSvg.title: Icon SVG
iconSvg.description: Inline SVG for the tile icon. Required only for new editors whose icon is not already shipped by xtralab.

rank.title: Rank
rank.description: Preference order (lower numbers come first). The launcher shows the first available editor by rank.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: When false, hides the editor from the launcher (and the Terminals panel stops badging it).

requireAvailable.title: Require available
requireAvailable.description: When false, the launcher skips the availability check for this entry (useful for a shell alias that isn't on PATH but resolves in an interactive shell). Overriding a built-in editor's command turns this off automatically, so an aliased command still shows; set it explicitly to force the check on or off.
